headline: Highest risk is medium: Chatwoot’s broad egress and customer-data handling can feed Pathway pipelines, creating leakage and cascading-error risks; no direct shared-channel evidence is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest external messages and has broad network egress, while Pathway has no direct input channel documented. A prompt-injection path is therefore not provably absent, but it would require an unusual bridge such as manual copy/paste or an undocumented shared workspace. Pathway’s no-IO profile reduces the blast radius.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are manually copied into Pathway prompts or rules, injection becomes plausible.
IF an undocumented shared filesystem or queue is added between them, attacker-controlled text can traverse the pair.
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between Chatwoot and Pathway.
Keep Pathway isolated from shared workspaces and message queues.
Add a review step before any Chatwoot text is transformed into Pathway instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all Chatwoot-derived content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and it has broad egress. Pathway is documented as a document-processing system with no filesystem or network IO surfaces exposed here, so leakage is not automatic, but if Chatwoot data is fed into Pathway pipelines the pair can expose sensitive customer content in default workflows.
conditions: IF Chatwoot customer records are routed into Pathway processing jobs, sensitive content can be replicated into downstream outputs.
IF Pathway is configured to emit processed documents to external sinks, customer data may leave the original support boundary.
mitigations: Restrict Pathway inputs to redacted Chatwoot exports.
Block customer messages and orders from any non-redacted pipeline.
Verify outbound destinations for both systems before enabling sync.
requires-engineering: implement field-level DLP on Chatwoot-to-Pathway transfers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress, but Pathway explicitly lacks filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and network egress capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only data flow, so the pair’s capability conflict is limited.
conditions: IF Pathway is wrapped by an external orchestrator that grants write access, conflict risk increases.
IF both agents are later pointed at the same mutable directory, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only relative to Chatwoot artifacts.
Avoid mounting the same writable directory into both systems.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: add locking if a shared mutable store is introduced.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot produces customer-support content and reports, and Pathway is a document-processing pipeline that could treat those outputs as authoritative inputs. Because no verification step is documented, errors or hallucinated summaries from Chatwoot can cascade into Pathway-derived documents or actions, though Pathway itself has no direct action-taking surface shown.
conditions: IF Pathway consumes Chatwoot-generated summaries without validation, upstream mistakes propagate downstream.
IF Pathway outputs are used as source material for customer-facing actions, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review of Chatwoot outputs before Pathway ingestion.
Add schema validation for all Chatwoot-derived records.
Compare Pathway outputs against original support tickets.
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance metadata end-to-end.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while Pathway’s residency, retention, and certification posture is not documented here. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated customer data is processed by Pathway without matching controls; uncertainty pushes this above low because the data class is sensitive and the pairwise policy gap is unknown.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is sent into Pathway, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF Pathway stores or logs those records under a different retention policy, deletion/export requests may fail.
mitigations: Classify Chatwoot data before any Pathway transfer.
Confirm retention and deletion handling on both sides.
Limit Pathway to de-identified or aggregated records.
requires-engineering: document a DPA and data-flow map for the pair.
